question: As a manager, how much more strongly do my reports react to a bad interaction with me than to a good one?
note: answer: six times more strongly than to a positive one

question: A proposal would make us more open but slow us down by about as much as it helps. Which value should win, and do we do it?
note: answer: yes, move ahead, because Transparency sits higher than Efficiency in the values hierarchy (the hierarchy is a weighting, not an automatic override)

question: One of the operating principles on the values page no longer seems to drive behavior. How do I get it taken off the page?
note: answer: submit a merge request explaining the reasons in its description; the GitLab Value Handbook Page owner must approve and merge it

question: When team members were surveyed about renaming the 'Brag Document', what share of them wanted a different title?
note: answer: 100% of those polled (in a TMRG channel survey), so the title was changed

question: How long does a Reverse AMA session last?
note: answer: 50 minutes (a closed Zoom call)

question: I'm part of an underrepresented group and would like to set up a Reverse AMA with an E-Group member. How do I get it started?

heading_path: Process for initiating a Reverse AMA

note: answer: create an issue and tag a DIB team member, the E-Group member's EBA and Stella Treas (Chief of Staff to the CEO); the E-Group member then reviews it and may accept, suggest another host such as a direct report, or reject it

question: What theme should the Engineering team use when picking a code name for a confidential project?
note: answer: hex color names

question: Why doesn't GitLab publish the scoring criteria it uses to evaluate job candidates?
note: answer: so candidates give an accurate overview of their experience and do not falsify their responses to meet the criteria (high-level interview plans are public)

question: Right before my Deep Dive call starts, which Slack channel can I use to let people know it is about to begin?
note: answer: #whats-happening-at-gitlab, with the Zoom and presentation links

question: According to the Power of the Pause guidance, what should a manager do before getting involved in a situation they think has gone wrong?
note: answer: understand the situation: take time to learn all the facts and sift out opinions and assumptions to uncover the truth, which can stop you creating a larger problem

question: A customer won't use Zoom and wants to meet on Microsoft Teams. How do I get a Teams or WebEx license?
note: answer: these licenses are only for team members with a business need to host meetings where Zoom is not accepted; create an access request and provide a justification

question: How early should the host and panelists join before a GitLab Zoom webinar begins?

heading_path: Everything you need to know about hosting or participating in a GitLab webinar

note: answer: 5 minutes before the start; only start livestreaming once everyone has joined

question: In GitLab's policies, what's the difference between "time off" and a "leave"?
note: answer: time off means shorter absences (vacation, sick days, public holidays) planned or used as needed; leave means longer, approved absences for specific life circumstances (e.g. parental or medical leave) that need a separate request and approval; the distinction is duration and purpose

question: After parental leave, how long does the reduced half-capacity return period usually last?
note: answer: the standard guideline is two to four weeks at reduced capacity, adjustable to individual needs

question: I live in Canada and we're expecting a baby. Where do I submit my parental leave request?
note: answer: US and Canada team members submit the request to Tilt (accessed through Okta), 30-45 days before the leave; Tilt takes 2-5 business days to build the personalized leave plan

question: Why does GitLab treat never taking vacation as a problem rather than a sign of dedication?

heading_path: GitLab's Philosophy to Time Away from Work
A Culture of Results and Sustainability

note: answer: it creates single points of failure, hinders documentation and knowledge sharing, and limits growth opportunities for colleagues who would otherwise step up

question: I'm joining GitLab partway through the year. How is my public holiday balance worked out?
note: answer: it is pro-rated from the hire date: (days remaining in the calendar year / 365) x the full-year public holiday entitlement, rounded to the nearest whole day (.5 and above rounds up), where local law permits

question: I'm based outside the US and my illness has kept me out for more than a week. What do I need to do?

heading_path: For Sick Absences that Exceed 6+ Consecutive Days

note: answer: 6+ days counts as a leave of absence: notify the Absence Management team with a Compass ticket, enter the time in Workday as "Out Sick", and provide supporting evidence per local requirements (e.g. medical certificate, doctor's note, fit note)

question: Do I have to show a death certificate or other documentation to take bereavement leave, and why?
note: answer: no; GitLab does not require documentation or proof of loss (unless local/statutory law requires it) because it trusts team members, which builds trust and supports them during vulnerable times

question: One of my reports is going on parental leave for about four months. How should I cover their work while they're out?

heading_path: General Guidelines For Managers on Resource Allocation

note: answer: for leave under 6 months, use internal resources (who may be eligible for an interim bonus) and/or consider hiring a temporary contractor

question: On a regular (not customer-billable) work trip, what's the daily limit for my own meals?
note: answer: up to $120 USD (or local currency equivalent) per day

question: A relative is putting me up during a work trip, so I'm skipping the hotel. Can I claim anything for that?
note: answer: yes, up to a $50 host/hostess gift

question: I lost the receipt for a work purchase. How can I still get it reimbursed?
note: answer: complete a Missing Receipt Affidavit (make a copy of the template) and attach it to the expense as a PDF when submitting

question: Why can't I expense my personal VPN subscription anymore?
note: answer: since July 15, 2026 GitLab uses one centrally managed VPN, NordLayer; it gives the same protection as a personal VPN while improving security oversight and access management, replacing a patchwork of individual subscriptions

question: How much emergency medical cost does GitLab's business travel insurance cover?

heading_path: Business Travel Emergency Support and Insurance

note: answer: up to $250,000 per occurrence

question: On travel that's billed back to the customer, do I need to keep receipts for my meals?
note: answer: no; unless the customer's SoW says otherwise, meals on billable travel are paid at the destination's per diem rate, and per-diem meal reimbursement needs no receipts

question: If nobody closes my onboarding issue, does it ever get closed on its own, and when?
note: answer: yes, the employment bot automatically closes any onboarding issue still open after 60 days

question: I've been at GitLab about five months and want to be an onboarding buddy. How do I get involved?

heading_path: How Can I Become An Onboarding Buddy?

note: answer: buddies are assigned by the new hire's manager; if you have been at GitLab 3+ months, tell your manager you are interested in the Onboarding Buddy Program

question: I'm stuck making my first handbook edit through a merge request. Who can help me, and how do I find them?
note: answer: a Merge Request Buddy; search the GitLab Team page for 'Merge Request Buddy' or ask in the #mr-buddies Slack channel

question: While setting up my new MacBook, why am I warned not to click into Gmail or Google Drive from the Okta dashboard right away?

heading_path: MacBook Step 1: Activate Your Okta Account

note: answer: opening Gmail or any Google app before finishing the laptop setup in Step 2 will lock you out of your laptop

question: What size USB stick do I need before I start setting up my Dell Linux laptop?
note: answer: a boot-capable USB drive of at least 8GB

question: Is there a price limit on the Dell laptop if I choose Linux instead of a Mac?
note: answer: yes, a Linux laptop may not cost more than the equivalent 16-inch MacBook Pro

question: My refresh laptop just arrived. What's the deadline for dealing with my old one?
note: answer: the old laptop must be wiped or returned within 2 weeks of receiving the replacement

question: My MacBook needs a repair. At what repair cost might IT decide to replace it instead of fixing it?
note: answer: if the repair will cost more than $1,000 USD (and/or take too long), IT may replace the laptop

question: I'm leaving GitLab before my first year is up and want to buy my work laptop. How do I start that?
note: answer: if the company agrees, email laptops@gitlab.com; the Manager of IT or Lead IT Analyst approves and emails the price (current net value), then accounting sends payment information

question: Why can't I use ngrok to give someone a public link to my local development environment?
note: answer: it exposes the laptop to the public Internet; because GitLab's product and other dev apps allow remote code execution, it would be a back-door for attackers that could compromise your home network and accounts, and it circumvents the firewall in violation of the Acceptable Use Policy

question: How long can my laptop sit idle before the screen saver has to lock it?
note: answer: 15 minutes or less

question: Why can't I just factory reset my laptop myself before handing it back, instead of booking time with IT?
note: answer: wipes must be done by an IT analyst with Jamf (macOS) or Fleet (Linux), which ensures a clean disk wipe and lets GitLab keep evidence of it; you may only wipe it yourself if IT asks, e.g. for troubleshooting

question: What's the longest expiration I'm allowed to set on an impersonation token?
note: answer: 24 hours

question: Revoking a leaked token right away could break our pipelines and integrations. Why does GitLab still revoke it immediately?
note: answer: the standard is immediate revocation followed by an investigation, because the impact of breaking existing access and automation is typically much smaller than the risk of a valid token being used by a malicious actor

question: Why does GitLab rate a YubiKey in FIDO2 mode or Touch ID higher for MFA than a code from an authenticator app like Google Authenticator?
note: answer: FIDO2 authenticators (e.g. a YubiKey in FIDO2 mode, Touch ID) are phishing-resistant: authentication is cryptographically bound to the relying party origin, so credentials cannot be replayed against a spoofed site; TOTP codes are not phishing-resistant (vulnerable to AiTM real-time phishing and seed theft), so they rank Low assurance versus High

question: I'm about to travel with my work laptop and phone. How should I set up my 1Password vaults for Travel Mode?
note: answer: none of the GitLab shared vaults are marked safe for travel, so create a dedicated travel vault or mark your Private vault as safe for travel, enable Travel Mode, then open 1Password on each device you take so it syncs and removes the other vaults

question: If a team member never turns on two-factor authentication, how long before their account gets blocked?

heading_path: Two factor authentication and time-based one time passwords

note: answer: users without 2FA enabled that are stale for over 30 days are blocked/suspended until resolved

question: What data classification level applies to team members' work email addresses?
note: answer: Yellow; an exception to Personal Data being Orange, covering team member names, work email addresses and GitLab usernames

question: I lost my YubiKey on the train. Who do I notify?
note: answer: send an email to panic@gitlab.com right away

question: I'm working a support ticket and need a customer's data on my laptop to reproduce the problem. Am I allowed to, and what conditions apply?
note: answer: yes, for an active customer support case only; delete the data immediately when the case is resolved (on macOS empty the Trash or use rm), and log and document all data handling in the ZenDesk ticket

question: How long do we have to keep records of system access reviews?
note: answer: 1 year 3 months, then GCP/AWS secure deletion

question: Under the security logging standard, what's the minimum retention for security logs from a critical system that isn't production?
note: answer: 90 days minimum (the separate 60-day row in the records retention table covers critical system activity logs, not security logs)

question: How often does GitLab check that the providers hosting its SaaS infrastructure meet physical security requirements?
note: answer: annually, as part of the Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) review and the Complementary User Entity Controls (CUEC) review

question: Does a configuration-only change need testing and approval before it goes to production, or is that just for code?
note: answer: yes; development work must be tested and approved before deployment to production, and this includes configuration changes and other related changes not considered development work

question: I have an idea for a new Informative Reference that maps to CSF 2.0. Which email address should I send it to?
note: answer: olir@nist.gov (other resource suggestions, such as QSG topics, go to cyberframework@nist.gov)

question: Why do the CSF 2.0 Subcategory numbers have gaps, for example there is no ID.AM-06?
note: answer: the numbering is intentionally not sequential; the gaps mark CSF 1.1 Subcategories that were relocated in CSF 2.0

question: Which CSF 2.0 Subcategory ID covers keeping data backups?
note: answer: PR.DS-11 (backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested)

question: Under CSF 2.0, once we have drafted both a Current Profile and a Target Profile, what should we do next?
note: answer: run a gap analysis between the Current and Target Profiles and develop a prioritized action plan (e.g., risk register, risk detail report, POA&M) to close the gaps, then implement it and update the Profile

question: What kinds of AI bias does the NIST AI RMF tell organizations to consider and manage?
note: answer: three categories: systemic, computational and statistical, and human-cognitive

question: According to the NIST AI RMF, what should happen to an AI system that is actually causing severe harm?
note: answer: its development and deployment should cease in a safe manner until the risks can be sufficiently managed

question: In the NIST AI RMF, after the GOVERN outcomes are in place, which function do most users start with?
note: answer: the MAP function, then on to MEASURE or MANAGE

question: How does the AI RMF tell transparency, explainability and interpretability apart?
note: answer: transparency answers what happened in the system; explainability answers how a decision was made; interpretability answers why a decision was made and its meaning or context to the user

question: Under NIST SP 800-88r2, what minimum security strength must the encryption have before cryptographic erase can be relied on?
note: answer: at least 128 bits (the ISO/IEC 27040 requirement for the algorithm and mode encrypting the target data)

question: How often should a system's confidentiality security categorization be revisited, according to SP 800-88r2?
note: answer: at least every three years, or when a significant change occurs in the system

question: In SP 800-88r2, which role keeps track of sanitized storage devices after they are handed to another team, given away, or destroyed?
note: answer: the property management officer

question: Why might cryptographic erase be unacceptable for data that has to stay confidential for decades?
note: answer: the data still sits on the media as ciphertext, so future weaknesses in the algorithms or new computing power (e.g., quantum computing) could make the keys, and so the data, recoverable

question: How soon must an employer notify OSHA when a worker is admitted to hospital as an inpatient after a work incident?
note: answer: within 24 hours (a work-related fatality must be reported within 8 hours)

question: Why does OSHA warn that mandatory drug testing after an injury can undermine a safety program?
note: answer: it can suppress reporting of injuries and illnesses, so hazards may remain undetected

question: Our budget won't cover every hazard control at once. How does OSHA suggest we decide which ones to put in first?
note: answer: implement on a worst-first basis using the hazard ranking (risk) from hazard identification and assessment; workers must still be protected from recognized serious hazards, and easy, inexpensive fixes should be done promptly

question: What simple rule of thumb does OSHA give for spotting excessive noise in a work area?
note: answer: an area where you must raise your voice to be heard by others

note: unanswerable: webinars.md covers roles, starting and post-webinar steps but no attendee cap or license size; searched webinar, attendee, participant, capacity, limit, maximum, seats, and numbers near webinar/zoom across the Markdown corpus and pdf-text

note: unanswerable: the sick time and caregiver sick time policies give each team member 25 paid days per rolling 12 months but never say whether days can be donated, transferred or pooled; searched corpus and pdf-text for donat, leave bank, leave sharing, shared leave, transfer sick/PTO days, sick days (only laptop donations and NIST media donation match)

note: unanswerable: the Acceptable Use Policy (Mobile Messaging) requires Slack for work conversations but no document gives a Slack retention period, and the records retention table has no Slack row; searched the corpus and pdf-text for slack near retain/retention/delet/days/history, message near retain/retention/kept for/deleted after/auto-delete, chat near retain/retention/delet/days, instant messag
